item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Sat Oct 31, 8:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Out of Line: Art at the Edge — Sat Oct 31, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
Inspired by conceptual artist Bruce Nauman’s video work “Dance or Exercise on the Perimeter of a Square (Square Dance), 1967–68,” this exhibition explores Davis as a site of both artistic practice and political protest. Mike Henderson, Ester Hernandez, Malaquías Montoya, Bruce Nauman, Nancy Rubins, Dorothy Wiley and the student artists of UC Davis’ Third World Forum engage with film, print and performance to confront who they were and what their work meant in a world of radical change. They made work wherever and however they could: in collaborative workshops, student newsrooms, kitchens and living rooms. While rooted in the politics of the late 20th century, “Out of Line” finds renewed meaning in the present day.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Sat Oct 31, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Birds & Bikes — Sat Oct 31, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: Axis Gallery is proud to announce Birds & Bikes, a collaborative art exhibition bringing together regional artists to explore the poetic intersections of avian flight and human motion. Running from October 2 through November 1, 2026, the exhibition showcases a dynamic range of works from intricate metal sculptures and imaginative textile art to curated gallery shop goods, celebrating the beauty of migration alongside the engineering of daily travel. The exhibition features a direct partnership with the City of Sacramento Office of Arts and Culture (OAC) Art in Public Places program and North Natomas Jibe. Birds & Bikes serves as an artistic tie-in to the upcoming Birds and Benches project, which will install artist-designed public benches across North Natomas Regional Park. Visitors are invited to experience the unique ecology and transit identity of the Natomas Basin through a collaborative lens, discover one-of-a-kind art pieces, and browse handcrafted items in the East Gallery Pop

item.title: Davis Craft and Vintage Fair — Sun Nov 1, 10:00 AM — Central Park – Davis
item.description:
Davis Craft and Vintage Fair began as the Square Tomatoes Craft Fair more than 10 years ago! The event was started by instructors from the UC Davis Craft Center in order to have a monthly craft fair for local artisans and the local community. We embraced local vintage vendors in 2017, we’ve grown and we are still home to local artists and makers from the Davis and greater Sacramento area. We collaborate with local non-profits starting with Couleurs Vives Art Studio who joined us in 2018! Many of our talented vendors can be found at other festivals like the Davis Phoenix Coalition’s Pride Fest, the I-House’s International Festival, and 2nd Friday ArtAbouts on E Street Plaza. Expect to see friendly vendors with local handmade and original art, crafts, quality vintage items, upcycled treasures, earth-friendly creations, good food, and more. Free live music fills the open space for a lively atmosphere so be sure to stop by and join us!
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Weave a Cattail Visor Sunhat — Sun Nov 1, 10:00 AM
item.description: In this hands-on workshop led by Samantha Iacobello, participants will learn simple, beginner friendly techniques such as plaiting, coiling, and sewing to weave a crownless, full brim sunhat using cattail gathered from Samantha’s local watersheds. Samantha Iacobello has been wild foraging basketry plants for weaving projects for the last six years and has been teaching for four years at her off-grid home in Calaveras county. She is an archaeobotanist, ecologist, conservationist, and a professional landscaper and arborist – all of which have contributed to her current passion of weaving baskets and other projects. All tools and materials will be provided. This workshop requires the ability and patience to do repetitive hand movements, and comfort sitting on the ground for extended periods of time. This offering is part of Davis Forest School’s Adult/Family workshops, and is open to ages 10+. Visit our website to learn more and to register. Spots are limited, and the last day to sign

item.title: Munchie Man: Grand Opening — Tue Nov 3, 2:30 AM
item.description:
There’s a new spot in Downtown Davis! Join us on November 3 to celebrate the grand opening of Munchie Man! The festivities kick off with a special ribbon-cutting ceremony hosted by the Davis Chamber of Commerce at 10:30 AM, followed by doors opening to the public at 11:00 AM. Come welcome Munchie Man to the downtown community and check out Davis’ newest addition! Learn more: www.munchiemandavis.com
Munchie Man started as a 2023 pop-up in East Sacramento and now in 2026 we are a “funky bistro” specializing in local craft beer & wine with small plates. Everything you’ll find here tells a story. The menu is inspired by my travels, the restaurants that left an impression on me, and the people and experiences that shaped who I am. In many ways, it’s an autobiography told through food. Some dishes are inspired by places I’ve visited, others by people I love, and a few simply exist because they make me smile. And I hope they make you smile too.
Source: Davis Downtown

item.description:

The series kicks off with One, Two, Three (1961), Billy Wilder’s fast-paced political comedy starring James Cagney, Horst Buchholz, and Arlene Francis. Davis Enterprise film critic Derrick Bang will introduce the film with behind-the-scenes insights and fun facts, followed by a Q&A after the screening. Enjoy live music by According to Bazooka before the movie! Admission and popcorn are FREE! Donations are welcome, and the bar will be open for beverage purchases. Doors open at 6:29 PM, and the movie begins at 7:01 PM. Everyone is welcome!

item.description:
The laughs continue at the Davis Odd Fellows Classic Film Fest with a screening of Mel Brooks’ comedy classic The Producers (1968)! Starring Zero Mostel and Gene Wilder, this outrageous comedy follows a scheming theater producer and a mild-mannered accountant who hatch a plan to make a fortune from a Broadway flop. Naturally, things don’t go quite as planned! Davis Enterprise film critic Derrick Bang will share fascinating film trivia and behind-the-scenes insights before the screening, followed by a Q&A afterward. We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

Native American Heritage Month recognizes the histories, cultures, contributions, and continuing presence of Native American, Alaska Native, and Indigenous peoples. It is an opportunity to learn from Indigenous communities, celebrate their diverse traditions, and recognize their enduring connections to their lands and cultures. Learn more at the Smithsonian Institution.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Manetti Shrem Museum: Together Again, 1960–2026, Perspectives from UC Davis’ Fine Arts Collection — Wed Nov 4, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description: Together Again inaugurates the Manetti Shrem Museum’s ongoing collection galleries. This exhibition highlighting the collection will be on long-term view, accompanied by temporary exhibitions each fall and winter. The ongoing collection galleries trace a history of art forged from UC Davis and throughout Northern California. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, this presentation proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri. Together Again builds bridges between who we were and who we are becoming at UC Davis, and affirms the Manetti Shrem Museum as home to the complex story of No

item.title: Diwali, Festival of Lights — Sun Nov 8 — CA
item.description:
Diwali is celebrated by many Hindus, Jains, Sikhs, and some Buddhists, with traditions that vary across communities. Often associated with light, hope, renewal, and the triumph of good over evil, the festival brings families and communities together. Learning about Diwali is one way to celebrate religious diversity and build understanding across cultures. Learn more here.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Jan 13, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants

item.title: DataLab Office Hours (in person) — Tue Jan 26, 1:00 PM — Shields Library
item.description:
DataLab offers free in person drop-in office hours during which UC Davis researchers can obtain data science help and advice on working with their data. During these short, just-in-time sessions we meet with faculty, students, postdoctoral scholars, and staff from all domains across the University. Depending on the nature of your question and our availability, it may be possible to schedule a longer follow-up consultation after your office hours visit.
Appointments are not required. Please complete the brief office hours intake form ahead of time to help us connect you with the right expert for your question.
Common office hours help topics include:
Open Source Programming (R, Python, Julia, etc.)Reproducible research computing and data scienceResponsible and ethical data scienceData gathering, organization, databases, and experimental designData analysis, statistics, and explorationData visualizationMachine learning and neural networksText mining and natural language processingGeos
